title: Elevating the Gravity of the Matter
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This essay tackles a specific communication problem: how leaders make one priority feel urgent and important amid a sea of competing projects, without sounding alarmist. It recommends using unconventional timing, settings, or message formats to signal that an issue is genuinely different — an evening meeting when that's not typical, or an unusual venue like a rooftop gathering — combined with explicit metrics connecting the issue to long-term outcomes. The core insight is that unexpectedness itself, not volume or repetition, is what breaks through competing priorities and captures team attention.
points: Argues that raising urgency without alarming people is a distinct communication skill, separate from simply repeating a message louder or more often.
Recommends unconventional timing and settings (evening meetings, rooftop gatherings) as deliberate signals that an issue is genuinely different.
Ties elevated urgency to concrete metrics linking the issue to long-term outcomes, not just tone or emphasis.
Identifies the unexpected — not frequency or volume — as the true mechanism that breaks through competing organizational priorities.
Frames the leader's job as engineering surprise deliberately, rather than relying on urgency language alone.
quotes: To cut through the noise and competition for focused attention, leaders must create emphasis without sounding an alarm.
Speaking in the evening, for example, when that is not typical, signals to everyone that something different is afoot. An uncommon venue can also create emphasis.
By highlighting the metrics being influenced by the issue, leaders can persuade others of the new importance of the initiative.
What these tactics share in common is the unexpected. When team members receive messages at times, settings, in formats, and with a frequency they don’t expect, they pay attention differently.
Creating emphasis or urgency and elevating the gravity of an issue requires an unconventional call to action.
